nodes.label: lookup
nodes.rationale: Looks up the transaction in ZainCash records. stage4_lookup/lookup.py match_transaction uses app/db/repository.py and the lookup_transaction tool.

nodes.label: Account KYC
nodes.rationale: Verification, account level, ID documents, limits, or changing account details. Team Account & Security, minimum P4, no transaction. Not for login_access.

nodes.label: Agent Dispute
nodes.rationale: Problem with a ZainCash agent or shop: cash-in or cash-out not credited, extra fee, or refused service. Team Agent Network, minimum P2, requires amount, and needs a transaction.

nodes.label: App Bug
nodes.rationale: The app crashes, errors, or a feature fails, with no money lost. Team Tech Support, minimum P3, no transaction. Not for failed_transfer or bill_payment.

nodes.label: Bill Payment
nodes.rationale: A bill or top-up failed or was not applied by the biller. Team Payments Ops, minimum P3, requires amount, and needs a transaction. Not for person-to-person failed_transfer.

nodes.label: Card Issue
nodes.rationale: ZainCash Mastercard or virtual card declined, blocked, not delivered, or charged twice. Team Cards, minimum P3, no transaction. Not for wallet failed_transfer.

nodes.label: Failed Transfer
nodes.rationale: A transfer that failed, stuck, or left the wallet but did not arrive. Team Payments Ops, minimum P2, requires amount and date, and needs a transaction. Not for wrong_recipient or bill_payment.

nodes.label: Fraud Report
nodes.rationale: Scam, OTP or PIN request, unauthorized transactions, or a hacked account. Team Account & Security, minimum P1, no transaction required. Not for simply forgetting a PIN.

nodes.label: General Inquiry
nodes.rationale: Questions about fees, limits, how to do something, agent locations, or promotions. Team General Care, minimum P4, no transaction. Not for a problem that already happened.

nodes.label: Login Access
nodes.rationale: Cannot log in, forgot PIN or password, verification code not arriving, or account locked. Team Account & Security, minimum P3, no transaction. Not for fraud_report.

nodes.label: Other
nodes.rationale: Anything that does not fit the other categories, including complaints with no clear request. Team General Care, minimum P4, no transaction. Unknown classifier labels are mapped here.

nodes.label: Refund Request
nodes.rationale: Money back from a merchant purchase or a cancelled service. Team Disputes, minimum P3, requires amount, and needs a transaction. Not for wrong_recipient or failed_transfer.

nodes.label: Support Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for categories, teams, and priorities, cited as spec section 4.

nodes.label: Wrong Recipient
nodes.rationale: Money sent to the wrong number or person by mistake. Team Disputes, minimum P2, requires amount, and needs a transaction. Not for a technical failed_transfer.

nodes.label: Priority Scale
nodes.rationale: P1 is money at risk now or fraud. P2 is money lost or stuck. P3 is a blocked service. P4 is an information request. Each category also has a minimum priority.

nodes.label: extract
nodes.rationale: Turns picks into a reference, amount, date, and phone. stage3_extract/extract.py finalize and fill_gaps verify spans so a value that is not in the ticket is dropped.

nodes.label: gemini_classify
nodes.rationale: Gemini structured output sampled three times. In cascade mode this same node runs combine() from stage2_classify/cascade.py to decide among Jev, Gemini, and a human.

nodes.label: jev_classify
nodes.rationale: Jev reads the ticket for category, priority, flags, and candidate picks, including a reversed-option check. Implemented in stage2_classify/jev.py through langchain-typesafe.

nodes.label: prepare
nodes.rationale: LangGraph node that cleans ticket text and finds candidate spans. stage1_normalize/normalize.py supplies normalize, mask_cards, and fold_arabic. candidates.py supplies recall-tuned find_candidates. dates.py resolve_date is used later during extract.

nodes.label: GeminiClassifier
nodes.rationale: Self-consistency over three samples at temperature 0.7. Confidence is the share of samples that agree on a taxonomy label. Invalid categories do not vote. A verbatim span that is not in the ticket is rejected so the model cannot invent a value.

nodes.label: JevClassifier
nodes.rationale: One main call asks category, priority, six flags, and candidate picks. A second call repeats category with the options reversed to catch position bias. Unknown categories become other and uncertain. Low top probability, low confidence, or an order disagreement also marks the ticket uncertain.

nodes.label: Gemini Classify Prompt v1
nodes.rationale: The ticket is untrusted customer text, so instructions inside it are ignored. Category must be one taxonomy id for the main problem. Priority follows P1 fraud or money at risk, P2 money lost or stuck, P3 blocked service, and P4 information. Spans must be copied character for character and values are never invented.

nodes.label: Gemini Extract Prompt v1
nodes.rationale: Returns only the requested fields and leaves the rest null. Amounts written in words, such as خمسين الف, normalize to a whole number of dinars. A verbatim span must occur in the ticket. The ticket text is untrusted and must not be followed as instructions.

nodes.label: Cascade Combine
nodes.rationale: Jev runs first, Gemini runs when Jev is unsure, and a human gets what is still uncertain. Gemini below T_GEM yields gemini_fallback with low_confidence. A confident Gemini that disagrees with Jev at or above 0.4 yields classifier_disagreement. Missing Jev degrades to Gemini. Missing Gemini keeps Jev. Both missing raises LLMUnavailable. A Jev pick at confidence 0.5 or higher beats the Gemini pick.

nodes.label: Pipeline Safety Constraints
nodes.rationale: An extracted field must be a substring of the ticket after digit conversion, or null. No code path sends a customer message. Card numbers are masked to the last four digits before storage. Tickets longer than MAX_STATE_CHARS (6000) are truncated before Jev.

nodes.label: Failure Handling
nodes.rationale: If Jev is down the run switches to Gemini-only and sets runs.degraded. If Gemini is down, Jev classification still completes and the draft is skipped with llm_unavailable. A span that is not in the text becomes null. Prompt injection is treated as untrusted data. multi_issue, a missing transaction, and an amount mismatch all escalate with a note and never ask for secrets.

nodes.label: pgvector Postgres Service
nodes.rationale: Image pgvector/pgvector:pg16 is published as host port 5433 because 5432 is already used by the local monster-mq project. Database, user, and password are support. docker/db/init.sql is mounted read-only into docker-entrypoint-initdb.d.

nodes.label: Support Pipeline Design
nodes.rationale: Agentic AI Challenge Iraq Topic 06. The product is a back-office batch pipeline, not a chatbot. Success is a live judge run, committed results for jev, gemini, and cascade, and the pre-scoring checks. Real customer data, real ZainCash integrations, sending messages, and cloud deployment are out of scope. Simple and reliable beats complex.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash
nodes.rationale: Second opinion on uncertain tickets and the fallback extractor, called through OpenRouter as google/gemini-3.8-flash. RAG drafting is planned for a later phase. The direct Google API was blocked on this network; OpenRouter was verified with the system CA bundle.

nodes.label: Jev
nodes.rationale: TypeSafe System One model used for fast, cheap classification. Its confidence scores are calibrated, and it picks extracted values from the ticket text so it cannot invent them.

nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.rationale: Gemini requests use https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 through langchain-openrouter. Unqualified gemini-* names are prefixed with google/. Costs use OpenRouter's reported charge when present; the token fallback defaults to $0.75 input and $3.75 output per million tokens.

nodes.label: ZainCash Support Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Back-office batch pipeline for Iraqi-dialect ZainCash tickets. It classifies, sets priority, extracts details, matches a transaction, routes to a team, and drafts a reply for a person to approve. It is not a chatbot and it never sends a reply on its own.

nodes.label: Idempotent Persistence
nodes.rationale: Tickets upsert on external_id and results upsert on (run_id, ticket_id), so a repeated batch does not duplicate rows. Knowledge-base tables are left out because Plan 3 PGVector manages its own tables. init_db still creates the vector extension. create_all is used instead of Alembic because the data is synthetic and resettable.

nodes.label: Cascade Classifier
nodes.rationale: Classification, extraction, routing, and escalation stay a fixed deterministic sequence. Jev runs first because it is calibrated and picks spans instead of generating them. Gemini self-consistency is the second opinion. If that is still uncertain, a person decides. A bounded tool-calling agent is used only for investigate-and-draft.

nodes.label: OpenRouter Provider Migration
nodes.rationale: The direct Google endpoint was blocked on the development network, so classification and extraction moved to OpenRouter and google/gemini-3.8-flash through langchain-openrouter, still behind StructuredLLM. OPENROUTER_API_KEY replaces GOOGLE_API_KEY for those calls. Jev stays pinned to jev-1.13.0. Reported cost takes precedence over the $0.75 / $3.75 token fallback.

nodes.label: Cascade Mode
nodes.rationale: Default run mode. Jev classifies first and Gemini is asked three times only when Jev is not confident. Cascade needs both TYPESAFE_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY. jev mode can still use OpenRouter for fallback extraction.

nodes.label: Support Workspace HTML Shell
nodes.rationale: Vite entry document. It mounts /src/main.tsx on #root and describes the product as classifying, routing, and reviewing Iraqi-Arabic tickets with a human in control.

nodes.label: Pipeline Graph Orchestration
nodes.rationale: graph.py builds the graph, runs a batch, and summarizes. state.py is LangGraph state. contracts.py holds shared dataclasses. factory.py wires real Jev and Gemini clients. io/serialize.py maps an outcome to a dict or database row.

nodes.label: Support Workspace
nodes.rationale: React, TypeScript, and shadcn/ui back office for Topic 06. Staff upload or paste Iraqi-dialect tickets, inspect evidence, and record review decisions. The UI does not implement its own classifier; model execution reuses pipeline/factory.py and pipeline/graph.py. API keys stay on the server.

nodes.label: Batch Runner
nodes.rationale: run_batch uses graph.abatch with a concurrency cap and return_exceptions so one failed ticket does not stop the batch. Empty text escalates with no model call. Confident Jev skips Gemini. A Jev failure in cascade mode degrades to Gemini.

nodes.label: support CLI
nodes.rationale: Typer app with init-db, seed-db, and run-batch. Modes are jev, gemini, and cascade. --no-db uses an in-memory transaction repo. The same pipeline code is what the later API and evaluation harness call.

nodes.label: Live Batch API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/runs returns 202 and reuses the compiled graph, outcome_from_state, summarize, and save_outcomes. A finished batch with ticket failures is completed_with_errors. Empty agent_trace means no tool calls were recorded. Requests are capped at 500 tickets and 10 MB.

nodes.label: Plan 1 Live Smoke
nodes.rationale: On 2026-10-07, in-memory jev, gemini, and cascade runs each processed five fixtures with no failures using google/gemini-3.8-flash. Two database cascade runs kept five ticket rows. These checks are connectivity tests; held-out accuracy is Plan 2.

nodes.label: Support Workspace UI Plan
nodes.rationale: Turn customer-support-ui into the Topic 06 workspace on the existing Python pipeline. Feature screens share typed API access. FastAPI services reuse the pipeline factory, graph, serializer, and PostgreSQL repository. Live data and illustrative preview data stay separate so the UI cannot invent a successful run.

nodes.label: Live Workspace
nodes.rationale: Uses FastAPI and PostgreSQL so runs, progress, documents, and reviews persist. Failed requests stay errors. The UI does not replace a failed live call with simulated success.

nodes.label: Pipeline Stage Strip
nodes.rationale: The One pipeline strip is an informational map from stages to implementation files. Clicking a stage opens a description. It does not execute the pipeline, and ticket details show only stage events the API actually recorded.

nodes.label: check_service_status
nodes.rationale: Checks known outages before the agent drafts a reply.

nodes.label: decide
nodes.rationale: Routes the ticket to a team and checks red flags. stage5_decide/rules.py decide and merge_reasons apply priority and escalation.

nodes.label: draft
nodes.rationale: Plan 3 stage. stage6_draft/agent.py and drafting.py use LangChain create_agent. guardrails.py checks the draft with a Jev requests_credentials noul plus regex. Knowledge search is a draft tool, not a separate graph node.

nodes.label: Five-Plan Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Plan 1 is the core pipeline and CLI. Plan 2 is synthetic data and evaluation. Plan 3 is knowledge-base RAG, the drafting agent, and guardrails. Plan 4 is FastAPI and the React review UI. Plan 5 is the weekly report, docs, CI, and the full compose stack.

nodes.label: Weekly Pattern Report
nodes.rationale: Stretch goal kept in scope. An issue is rising when this week is at least 1.5 times last week, there are at least five tickets, and a Poisson test gives p < 0.05. Clusters of matched transactions are checked against service incidents, then a Jev noul and a Gemini narrative that must cite counts and ticket ids.

nodes.label: Plan 1 Part 2
nodes.rationale: Continues the core pipeline plan with the Jev and Gemini classifiers, cascade combine rules, span-anchored extraction, transaction lookup, and routing. The header, global constraints, and review focus from part 1 apply here too.

nodes.label: Plan 1 Core Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Build a command-line batch pipeline that normalizes Iraqi-dialect tickets, classifies them, extracts details without inventing values, matches mock transactions, applies routing rules, and persists results to Postgres.

nodes.label: Bounded Drafting Agent
nodes.rationale: The agent is limited to six tool calls and 30 seconds and must finish by calling submit_draft. The ticket is wrapped as untrusted data. Tools only read data except flag_for_human and submit_draft, which record the agent's own output. Every call is stored on agent_trace.

nodes.label: Draft Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Citations must be chunks retrieved in this run. Amounts, references, dates, and phones in the draft must appear in the ticket or the matched transaction. The draft must not ask for an OTP, PIN, or password, checked by regex and a Jev requests_credentials noul below 0.2, and it must be Arabic of at most 120 words. A failed check keeps the draft and escalates with draft_failed_guardrail.

nodes.label: search_knowledge_base
nodes.rationale: Retrieves pgvector policy chunks so a draft can cite them.

nodes.label: Workspace NullDrafter Boundary
nodes.rationale: Generated drafts are not connected because the backend uses NullDrafter, so a reviewer writes the reply. Uploaded documents show Awaiting indexing because RAG retrieval is not connected. Weekly counts are real; evaluation only displays an imported report and does not run a model eval.

nodes.label: NullDrafter
nodes.rationale: Plan 1 drafter returns an empty DraftResult and adds no escalation reasons. Plan 3 replaces it with the RAG agent. Shipping a no-op keeps the graph shape stable before drafting exists.

nodes.label: NullDrafter
nodes.rationale: Plan 1 reply generation still uses NullDrafter. RAG drafting is Plan 3, so the verified pipeline does not yet write customer replies.

nodes.label: Preview Workspace
nodes.rationale: Uses labelled fixtures in src/data/preview.ts. Edits stay in the session and never call live mutations. Preview data is not measured output and is not the hackathon held-out dataset.

nodes.label: Awaiting Indexing
nodes.rationale: This slice stores PDF, Markdown, and text uploads with checksum deduplication and labels them Awaiting indexing. Embedding and RAG drafting stay separate backend work so the UI does not present stored files as retrievable knowledge.

nodes.label: Synthetic Data and Held-Out Split
nodes.rationale: All data is synthetic. About 300 tickets are split 200 dev and 100 test with seed 42, and test.sha256 is committed before any tuning. Prompts and thresholds are tuned on dev only. Gemini both generates the tickets and judges drafts; that bias is disclosed and human ratings are the counterweight.

nodes.label: Verified Capability Boundaries
nodes.rationale: NullDrafter does not generate replies. Document storage does not embed files into pgvector. The evaluation screen views imported reports and does not run a held-out evaluator. Those limits are shown in the UI and documented in the workspace README. Live and preview state stay separate so preview data is never reported as measured model output.

nodes.label: Taxonomy Specification
nodes.rationale: data/taxonomy.yaml is the single source of truth for categories, teams, and priorities. Hard overrides: fraud_suspected above 0.5 sets P1, and money_lost above 0.5 sets priority to at least P2.

nodes.label: Routing and Escalation Rules
nodes.rationale: Team comes from the category. fraud_suspected above 0.5 forces P1. money_lost above 0.5 raises priority to at least P2, then the category minimum applies. Any reason escalates the ticket and note_for writes a one-line reviewer note. Empty tickets escalate as empty_ticket at P4 without a model call.

nodes.label: Span-Anchored Extraction
nodes.rationale: finalize anchors every value to a span and normalizes reference, amount, phone, and date in code. fill_gaps calls Gemini only for weak required fields, and a Gemini failure leaves the original extraction. A value that was not stated is null. This implements spec section 6.3.

nodes.label: Transaction Lookup
nodes.rationale: Categories that do not need a transaction return not_applicable. Otherwise an exact reference is tried first, then phone plus amount within 1 percent and a three-day window. Several hits stay ambiguous unless a counterpart phone narrows them. Amount and date mismatches are separate statuses.

nodes.label: Classification Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Jev is pinned to jev-1.13.0 and jev-latest is forbidden because thresholds are tuned to a specific version. Defaults are T_JEV 0.6, T_GEM 0.66, and JEV_MIN_TOP_PROB 0.60. T_GEM 0.66 is chosen so two of three Gemini samples agreeing counts as confident.

nodes.label: Schema and Lookup Deviations
nodes.rationale: ambiguous was added for several matching transactions and escalates as txn_ambiguous. date_mismatch escalates too. T_GEM is 0.66 rather than 0.67 so two of three agreeing samples pass, which was the intent of the original threshold. Jev priority is read from the most likely Score level because score is an expected value. Schema changes use create_all instead of Alembic because the data is synthetic and resettable.

nodes.label: Red-Flag Escalation
nodes.rationale: Escalate when there is fraud, several issues, missing information, a transaction that was not found, or an amount mismatch. A draft must cite policy, must not invent numbers, and must never ask for an OTP or PIN.

nodes.label: Review API
nodes.rationale: Approval requires nonempty final text. Editing alone does not approve. Reassignment is its own review action. expected_updated_at and row locking reject stale concurrent edits. Human approval never sends a message, and API keys never reach the browser.

nodes.label: Workspace UI Verification
nodes.rationale: Records the implemented UI and live API. Backend pytest reported 134 passed, frontend tests 6 passed, and browser checks covered preview isolation, a one-ticket Jev run, a saved review that survived reload, document upload and deletion, and a 390px layout.

nodes.label: No Send Path
nodes.rationale: Results are saved as pending_review or escalated. There is no send path anywhere. Review actions write to reviews. An approved reply is available only through Copy approved reply.

nodes.label: Independent Review Fixes
nodes.rationale: Conflicting ticket content is rejected after re-reading durable rows, and the graph runs on the persisted text. Preview uploads are disabled. The reply editor stays mounted so unsaved text survives reassignment. Summaries count only committed outcomes. Queues over 500 tickets load every API page before client filtering or export.

nodes.label: Human Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Every path ends with a person. If the pipeline is unsure, or a safety check fails, it escalates with a short note. The agent approves, edits, or rejects, and only then sends the reply. Nothing is sent automatically.

nodes.label: LangGraph StateGraph
nodes.rationale: One node per stage: prepare, jev_classify, gemini_classify, extract, lookup, decide, and draft. Plain unit-tested Python functions choose the next node so routing stays testable instead of hiding inside the model.

nodes.label: Model Protocols and Fakes
nodes.rationale: Jev is reached through langchain-typesafe and Gemini through structured output. Each client sits behind a small protocol so unit tests use fakes and do not call the network. langchain-typesafe is pinned at 0.0.1a3 because it is alpha.

nodes.label: LangGraph Orchestration Decision
nodes.rationale: The fixed stages become a LangGraph StateGraph so routing stays plain Python and a batch uses graph.abatch with return_exceptions and RetryPolicy. This replaces the hand-written semaphore and retry loop in section 6.8. langchain-typesafe is used instead of the raw SDK and is wrapped behind the Classifier interface because the package is alpha.

nodes.label: flag_for_human
nodes.rationale: Records an escalation reason from inside the drafting agent.

nodes.label: get_customer_recent_transactions
nodes.rationale: Recent customer activity used as drafting context.

nodes.label: get_customer_ticket_history
nodes.rationale: Prior tickets for the same customer, used to spot repeat contacts.

nodes.label: lookup_transaction
nodes.rationale: Exact transaction-reference lookup for the drafting agent.

nodes.label: search_transactions
nodes.rationale: Fuzzy transaction search when the ticket has no reference.

nodes.label: submit_draft
nodes.rationale: Terminal drafting tool that records the reply. The agent is required to finish by calling it.
